about:
# MacroKit

Adds ready-made macros for your class and talent spec to your macro list, and keeps them up to date as you level, train and respec. An addon for World of Warcraft: Forever (client 1.60.x), with macros for all nine classes.

## What it does

MacroKit adds macros to your character's own macro list (`/macro`, the character tab) as soon as your character knows the spells they use.

- **It leaves room for your own macros.** Adding by itself always keeps 3 of your 18 character macro slots free, for macros you make and other addons' (such as GamepadMacros' heal macros), and says once which macros it held back. Add those from the window if you want them.
- **One button for all your buffs:** the **Missing Buff** macro casts whatever the missing-buffs row would cast first; press it again for the next. Offered in every class's list, added only when you ask.

- **It keeps up as you level.** When you level up, train at a trainer or learn a talent, it looks again straight away: macros you can now use are added (or, with automatic adding off, announced once in chat), the window updates, and a red badge on the minimap button counts what is new since you last opened the window. New macros are marked New in the window.
- **It knows your spec from your talents.** Forever has talent trees rather than a specialization choice, so MacroKit reads how many points you have in each tree (the same way the game's own talent window does) and takes the tree with the most. Before your first talent point, pick your spec in the window's menu; MacroKit remembers it for that character.
- **It follows a respec, a reset and a dual-spec switch.** It switches to the new spec's macros and says so in chat. The macros it added for your old spec are not deleted by themselves: the window offers a **Clear them** button (or type `/macrokit clear`).
- **Shows your missing buffs:** a row of glowing icons for the self-buffs your class should have up but does not, or that are about to run out, and for gathering tracking (Find Herbs, Find Minerals and the like) that is switched off. Click (or tap) one to cast it on yourself; it disappears straight away, in combat too. Move it with the **Position** button in the window (it steps through set spots on screen, easy with a gamepad) or Shift-drag it; turn it off in the window or with `/macrokit buffs`.
- **The hunter's Pet macro feeds your pet when it is not happy** (Feed Pet with the best food in your bags; Shift to Mend Pet), and remembers foods your pet refuses.
- **A starting attack for every class from level 1** (Lightning Bolt, Fireball, Frostbolt, Missiles, Shadow Bolt, Wrath, Smite, Shoot, alongside Strike, Opener and Holy Strike): with no enemy targeted, it targets the nearest one first, so one button starts a fight; handy on a controller.
- **Attack macros also start your auto-attack**, so a press still starts you swinging when you are out of rage, energy or mana. For hunters at range it starts Auto Shot. Crowd control that breaks on damage, such as Sap or Polymorph, does not.
- It never overwrites a macro: if you already have one with the same name, yours stays. (The one exception: a macro MacroKit itself added, still exactly as it added it, is brought up to date when MacroKit improves it.)
- It stops when your character's macro slots are full, and tells you which macros did not fit.
- In combat it waits until the fight is over, because the game does not allow creating macros in combat.

## The MacroKit window

Click the MacroKit button on the minimap, or type `/macrokit`.

- **Top:** your class, in its colour, and a **Spec** menu: Every spec (the macros all specs share), Holy, Protection or Retribution. It follows your talents; before you have any, pick your spec there. You can also pick another spec to look at its macros.
- **Ready to use** tab: macros whose spells you know. Those **in your macros** have a **To bar** button that puts them on the first empty button of your action bars (or drag them there); those **ready to add** have an **Add** button. Rows say *On your bars* once they're there.
- **Not learned yet** tab: macros waiting on a spell, each saying which. Learn the spell and the macro moves to Ready to use by itself, even with the window open.
- Hover over a macro to see how it works, in the **How it works** panel under the list and in its tooltip, along with the macro's text. At the bottom: **Add all missing**, **Remove MacroKit's macros** (press it twice), and the switch for adding new macros by themselves. The buttons are greyed out in combat, when the game does not allow changing macros.

Classes without macros yet are told so. The window remembers where you drag it and shrinks to fit a small screen. Drag the minimap button round the edge of the minimap to move it. MacroKit is also in Esc > Options > AddOns, and has a key binding to open the window (Options > Keybindings > AddOns).

## Getting a macro onto your action bar

1. Click the MacroKit button on the minimap (or type `/macrokit`).
2. On the **Ready to use** tab, find the macro. If it says *Ready to add*, click **Add**: it goes into your macro list and then says *In your macros*.
3. Click **To bar**: it goes on the first empty button of your action bars. Or drag the line from the MacroKit window onto any action bar slot (or click it once to pick it up, then click the slot).
4. You can also open the game's own macro window with `/macro`: MacroKit's macros are on the **character** tab, and you drag them from there the same way.

With "Add new macros by themselves" ticked, step 2 is done for you. It starts off for a new install, so nothing goes in your macro list until you choose; tick it in the window to have MacroKit add macros as you learn their spells.

The window shows these steps too, in its panel under the list, until you hover over a macro.

Once a macro is on your bar, hovering its button shows the spell's tooltip as usual, with MacroKit's explanation of what the macro does underneath. Turn that off with `/macrokit tooltips`.

Playing with a controller or on a Steam Deck? The gamepad macros (heal yourself, use a quest item, save and wear gear, leave a group, emotes) are in their own addon, [GamepadMacros](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gamepadmacros).

## Macros for every class

Each class has macros for every spec, plus a few for each talent tree. Hover a macro in the window to read exactly how it works. Most use the same pattern: a heal or buff goes on the friend under your mouse, else your friendly target, else you; an attack goes on the enemy under your mouse, else your target.

**Warrior**

- Every spec: Charge, Victory Rush, Strike, Rend, Hamstring, Interrupt, Overpower, Execute, Taunt, Shout.
- Arms: Mortal Strike, Sweeping, Spearing.
- Fury: Bloodthirst, Death Wish, Whirlwind.
- Protection: Shield Slam, Revenge, Shield Block, Last Stand.

**Paladin**

- Every spec: Holy Strike, Seal, Heal, Quick Heal, Might, Stun, Protect Ally, Freedom, Lay on Hands, Bubble, Dispel, Rez, Exorcism.
- Holy: Holy Shock, Big Heal, Oath, Vigil.
- Protection: Tank Up, Taunt, Swift Judge, Bulwark.
- Retribution: Command, Repent, Execute.

**Hunter**

- Every spec: Shoot, Mark, Sting, Arcane Shot, Aimed Shot, Multi-Shot, Concussive, Pet, Trap, Melee, Aspect, Lacerate.
- Beast Mastery: Bestial Wrath, Intimidation, Hawk.
- Marksmanship: Scatter Shot, Sniper Shot.
- Survival: Deterrence, Counterattack, Strider Kick.

**Rogue**

- Every spec: Opener, Stun, Interrupt, Stealth, Sap, Finisher, Shank, Blind.
- Assassination: Mutilate, Cold Eviscerate.
- Combat: Burst, Riposte.
- Subtlety: Hemorrhage, Ghostly Strike, Premeditation, Death Mark.

**Priest**

- Every spec: Shield, Renew, Flash Heal, Big Heal, Fortitude, Dispel, Cure, Smite, Mind Blast, SW: Pain, SW: Death, Fear Ward, Shackle, Rez. Smite targets the nearest enemy if you have none; Big Heal is Lesser Heal from level 1, then Heal, then Greater Heal.
- Discipline: Penance, Power Infusion, Focus Heal, Holy Fire.
- Holy: Mending, Group Heal, Holy Fire.
- Shadow: Shadowform, Silence, Vamp Embrace, Mind Flay.

**Shaman**

- Every spec: Lightning Bolt, Heal, Quick Heal, Chain Heal, Interrupt, Flame Shock, Frost Shock, Purge, Cure, Totems, Recall, Shield, Ghost Wolf, Rez.
- Elemental: Mastery Bolt, Chain Lightning.
- Enhancement: Stormstrike, Farseer.
- Restoration: Riptide, Swift Heal.

**Mage**

- Every spec: Fireball, Frostbolt, Missiles, Sheep, Counterspell, Decurse, Intellect, Conjure, Fire Blast, Slow Fall, Frostfire.
- Arcane: Arcane Blast, Burst, Quick Blast.
- Fire: Pyroblast, Combustion, Blast Wave.
- Frost: Ice Lance, Ice Block, Ice Barrier.

**Warlock**

- Every spec: Shadow Bolt, Corruption, Agony, Curse, Immolate, Fear, Banish, Drain, Death Coil.
- Affliction: Siphon Life, Exhaustion, Big Agony, Wrack.
- Demonology: Quick Demon, Sacrifice, Soul Link.
- Destruction: Conflagrate, Shadowburn, Havoc, Incinerate.

**Druid**

- Every spec: Wrath, Heal, Rejuv, Regrowth, Mark, Thorns, Decurse, Cure Poison, Innervate, Battle Rez, Rez, Roots, Hibernate, Faerie Fire, Moonfire.
- Balance: Moonkin, Insect Swarm.
- Feral Combat: Feral Charge, Lacerate, Primal Bite.
- Restoration: Swiftmend, Wild Growth, Swift Heal.

## Commands

| What | How |
|---|---|
| Open the MacroKit window | `/macrokit`, the minimap button, or MacroKit's entry in the minimap's addon list |
| Add the macros you are missing | `/macrokit add` |
| Show or hide your missing buffs | `/macrokit buffs` |
| Move the missing-buffs row to the next spot on screen | `/macrokit buffs move` (`/macrokit buffs reset`: back to the first) |
| See the macros and whether you have them, in chat | `/macrokit list` |
| Show or hide the minimap button | `/macrokit button` |
| Explain MacroKit's macros in action button tooltips, on or off | `/macrokit tooltips` |
| List your spec and spellbook, to report a spell name | `/macrokit spells` |
| See what the game reports about your talents | `/macrokit talents` |
| Delete the macros MacroKit added for a spec you are no longer | `/macrokit clear` |
| Delete the macros MacroKit added | `/macrokit remove` (macros you made yourself stay) |
| Add new macros by themselves, or stop (they are announced instead) | `/macrokit auto on`, `/macrokit auto off` |
| Version and key facts, for a bug report | `/macrokit debug`, then paste it in an [issue](https://github.com/bizzal70/MacroKit/issues) |

## Good to know

- Macros are saved on Blizzard's servers, so once added they follow your character to any computer, even without the addon.
- The spell names are Forever's, from spell lists built from the live game and checked against each other. Only the paladin's early spells have been checked in game so far. If a macro says it needs a spell you know you have, type `/macrokit spells` and please report what it lists.

## Controller

With a game controller, the **B** button closes the MacroKit window, like the X and Escape do. While a window is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B goes back to whatever you have it set to. When a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with the window open.

## More from this author

Other small addons for World of Warcraft: Forever, all free:

- **[GatherLog](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/gatherlog)** remembers ore, herbs, fishing pools, skinning spots, chests and rares across all your characters, and guides you back to the best spots.
- **[MouseTip](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/mousetip)** shows tooltips at your mouse cursor.
- **[RangeShade](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/rangeshade)** shades action buttons red when your target is out of range.
- **[JunkMate](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/junkmate)** sells junk and repairs at vendors, makes room for loot when your bags are full, and tidies your bank.
- **[AltGlance](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/altglance)** shows all your characters at a glance: level, gold, rested and where you left them.
- **[SwiftQuest](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/swiftquest)** accepts quests and hands them in as soon as you talk to the quest giver, without ever choosing a reward for you.
- **[SessionRecap](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/sessionrecap)** keeps a running tally of your play session: gold, experience per hour, quests, gathering and loot.
- **[ZoomPad](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/zoompad)** puts big + and - buttons on screen that zoom the camera, made for the Steam Deck touchscreen.
- **[FDR - Flight Data Recorder](https://www.curseforge.com/wow/addons/fdr-flight-data-recorder)** times every flight-master flight and counts your next one down to landing.

## Installing

Copy this folder into `World of Warcraft\_forever_\Interface\AddOns\` as `MacroKit`, restart the game, and enable MacroKit on the character select screen.

## Developing

- `tools\Link-Addon.ps1` links this folder into the game's AddOns folder, so edits are live after `/reload`.
- `python tests/run.py` runs the tests (`pip install lupa` once). They run the addon in real Lua 5.1 against a fake of the game's API.
- `tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "..."` runs the tests and pushes to GitHub. GitHub runs the tests again on every push.
- Macros live in `Data.lua`, by class and specialization ID. Adding another class means adding its table there; the tests check every macro's length, name and spells.

## Releasing

`tools\Publish.ps1 -Message "Release x.y.z" -Tag vx.y.z` publishes and tags. The tag makes GitHub package the addon and attach the zip to a GitHub release, and upload it to CurseForge once `## X-Curse-Project-ID:` is in `MacroKit.toc` and the CurseForge token is in this repository's secrets.

Before each release: raise `## Version:` in `MacroKit.toc` and add the version to `CHANGELOG.md`.

## Licence

MIT. See `LICENSE`.

# MacroKit

## 0.14.0

- **Keeps room for your own macros:** adding macros by itself now always leaves 3 of your 18 character macro slots free, for macros you make and other addons' (GamepadMacros' Heal Me, Heal Nearest and Buff Nearest). It says once which macros it held back; add them from the window if you want them.
- **To bar:** a macro in your list but not on your bars has a To bar button that puts it on the first empty action button on screen. No dragging, which is the hard part with a controller. Rows say "On your bars" once it's there.
- **New macro, Missing Buff:** casts whatever the missing-buffs row would cast first; press it again for the next. Put it on one controller button and buffing is one button. It's offered in every class's list and only added when you ask.
- **New installs start with adding by itself off,** so nothing lands in a new player's macro list unasked; existing players keep their setting. A one-time welcome line says what MacroKit does.
- **Remove asks you to press it twice,** so a slip can't delete your macros.
- The window remembers where you put it, and shrinks to fit a small screen.
- MacroKit is listed in Options > AddOns, and has a key binding to open its window.
- `/macrokit debug` prints the version and key facts for a bug report.

## 0.13.0

- **Starting attacks for every class:** new macros for the first attack each class learns: **Lightning Bolt** (shaman), **Fireball**, **Frostbolt** and **Missiles** (mage), **Shadow Bolt** (warlock, also sends your demon in), **Wrath** (druid) and **Shoot** (hunter: Auto Shot plus your pet). Like the others, they cast on the enemy under your mouse, else your target, and start your auto-attack. If you have no enemy targeted, they target the nearest one first, so one button starts a fight; handy on a controller. Warriors, rogues and paladins already had theirs (Strike, Opener, Holy Strike).
- **Priests:** Smite targets the nearest enemy in the same way, and **Big Heal** now works from level 1: Lesser Heal until you learn Heal (16), then Heal until Greater Heal (40). Macros you already have are brought up to date unless you changed them.

## 0.12.1

- **Controller:** when a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with a MacroKit window open (it used to stay on closing the window until the fight ended). It closes the window again once the fight is over.

## 0.12.0

- **Gathering tracking in the missing-buffs row:** Find Herbs, Find Minerals, Find Fish and Find Treasure, whichever you have learned, show in the row whenever their minimap tracking is switched off. Click (or tap) one to switch it back on. Any class.

## 0.11.9

- **Controller:** the B button now closes MacroKit's window, like the X and Escape. While one is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B does whatever you have it set to again.

## 0.11.8

- MacroKit now remembers the exact text it gave each macro it added, so any later improvement to a macro reaches yours: when you log in (and after levelling, training or a respec), each one still exactly as MacroKit last wrote it is brought up to date, and chat says which. A macro you have changed yourself is still left alone. Before, only the 0.8.0 auto-attack change could be carried over this way.

## 0.11.7

- The missing-buffs icons now show the cooldown sweep in combat too. In combat the game hides cooldowns from addons, so MacroKit hands them straight to the sweep, which can still draw them. Greying out and ignoring taps stay out of combat only: the game does not allow either in combat.

## 0.11.6

- Fixed: the missing-buffs icons did not grey out or show the cooldown sweep. Forever does not report the global cooldown on its own (spell 61304 does not exist there), so each icon now reads its own buff spell's cooldown, which includes the global cooldown. A buff with a cooldown of its own also stays greyed until it is ready.

## 0.11.5

- The missing-buffs icons show the global cooldown sweep, and out of combat they are greyed and ignore taps while it runs, so a tap too soon no longer makes an icon vanish with "Spell is not ready yet". In combat the game does not let addons switch them off, so only the sweep shows; wait for it before tapping. They are always switched back on as combat starts.

## 0.11.4

- A tapped buff icon whose cast fails ("Spell is not ready yet", out of mana, interrupted) now comes straight back out of combat, instead of a few seconds later. In combat the game does not let addons show it again, so it comes back when the fight ends.

## 0.11.3

- An icon in the missing-buffs row now disappears as soon as you click (or tap) it, in combat too, so you can see what is left to cast. If the cast did not work (out of mana, too soon), the icon comes back after combat, or within a few seconds out of combat.

## 0.11.2

- Fixed: clicking an icon in the missing-buffs row did nothing. The game's "cast on key down" setting (on by default) makes click-to-cast buttons ignore a release on its own; the icons now take the press too.

## 0.11.1

- The missing-buffs row can be moved with a gamepad: the new **Position** button in the MacroKit window (or `/macrokit buffs move`) steps it through set spots on screen: above the middle, below the middle, the top, the bottom above the bars, left and right of the middle. After each step the row shows for a few seconds, even with no buff missing, so you can see where it is. Shift-drag still places it anywhere with a mouse.

## 0.11.0

- New: **missing buffs**. A row of glowing icons near the middle of the screen shows the self-buffs your class should have up but does not (for example Inner Fire and Power Word: Fortitude, Arcane Intellect and an armor, an aspect, Battle Shout, a shaman's shield and weapon imbue), or that have under 2 minutes left (30 seconds for short buffs). Click an icon to cast it on yourself. Only learned spells are asked for, any version of a buff counts (any armor, the group Fortitude), and it stays quiet while mounted, dead or on a flight. In combat it waits, as the game allows no changes then. Shift-drag to move it; turn it off with the new tick box in the window or `/macrokit buffs`.

## 0.10.2

- The wand lines from 0.10.0 and 0.10.1 are gone again: they got in the way of a caster's rotation. Caster attack macros are back to a plain `/startattack`; put your wand (Shoot) on a key of its own. Macros already in your list go back the next time you log in, unless you changed them.

## 0.10.1

- Fixed: the wand line cancelled spells with a cast time or a channel (Mind Blast, Smite, Holy Fire, Mind Flay, Penance, Frostfire Bolt, Arcane Blast, Pyroblast, Corruption, Immolate, Drain, Wrack, Incinerate), because starting Shoot interrupts a spell still being cast. Only instant attack macros start the wand now; the others still swing in melee when no wand is equipped. Macros already in your list are updated the next time you log in, unless you changed them.

## 0.10.0

- Mages, priests and warlocks: attack macros now shoot your **wand** (Shoot) when one is equipped, and swing your melee weapon only when none is. In Forever, `/startattack` swings the melee weapon even with a wand equipped. The warlock's Curse macro only shoots the wand, since both lines would take it past the game's 255 characters. Caster macros already in your list are updated the next time you log in, unless you changed them.

## 0.9.2

- Priests get **Mind Blast** (every spec) and **Holy Fire** (Discipline and Holy; Shadow priests rarely use it, and it would take a Shadow priest past 18 macros). Both cast on the enemy under your mouse, else your target, and start your auto-attack.

## 0.9.1

- Priests get a **Smite** macro: Smite on the enemy under your mouse, else your target, starting your auto-attack like the other attack macros.

## 0.7.0

# MacroKit

## 0.12.1

- **Controller:** when a fight starts, B goes straight back to its usual job, even with a MacroKit window open (it used to stay on closing the window until the fight ended). It closes the window again once the fight is over.

## 0.12.0

- **Gathering tracking in the missing-buffs row:** Find Herbs, Find Minerals, Find Fish and Find Treasure, whichever you have learned, show in the row whenever their minimap tracking is switched off. Click (or tap) one to switch it back on. Any class.

## 0.11.9

- **Controller:** the B button now closes MacroKit's window, like the X and Escape. While one is open, B closes it; once it is closed, B does whatever you have it set to again.

## 0.11.8

- MacroKit now remembers the exact text it gave each macro it added, so any later improvement to a macro reaches yours: when you log in (and after levelling, training or a respec), each one still exactly as MacroKit last wrote it is brought up to date, and chat says which. A macro you have changed yourself is still left alone. Before, only the 0.8.0 auto-attack change could be carried over this way.

## 0.11.7

- The missing-buffs icons now show the cooldown sweep in combat too. In combat the game hides cooldowns from addons, so MacroKit hands them straight to the sweep, which can still draw them. Greying out and ignoring taps stay out of combat only: the game does not allow either in combat.

## 0.11.6

- Fixed: the missing-buffs icons did not grey out or show the cooldown sweep. Forever does not report the global cooldown on its own (spell 61304 does not exist there), so each icon now reads its own buff spell's cooldown, which includes the global cooldown. A buff with a cooldown of its own also stays greyed until it is ready.

## 0.11.5

- The missing-buffs icons show the global cooldown sweep, and out of combat they are greyed and ignore taps while it runs, so a tap too soon no longer makes an icon vanish with "Spell is not ready yet". In combat the game does not let addons switch them off, so only the sweep shows; wait for it before tapping. They are always switched back on as combat starts.

## 0.11.4

- A tapped buff icon whose cast fails ("Spell is not ready yet", out of mana, interrupted) now comes straight back out of combat, instead of a few seconds later. In combat the game does not let addons show it again, so it comes back when the fight ends.

## 0.11.3

- An icon in the missing-buffs row now disappears as soon as you click (or tap) it, in combat too, so you can see what is left to cast. If the cast did not work (out of mana, too soon), the icon comes back after combat, or within a few seconds out of combat.

## 0.11.2

- Fixed: clicking an icon in the missing-buffs row did nothing. The game's "cast on key down" setting (on by default) makes click-to-cast buttons ignore a release on its own; the icons now take the press too.

## 0.11.1

- The missing-buffs row can be moved with a gamepad: the new **Position** button in the MacroKit window (or `/macrokit buffs move`) steps it through set spots on screen: above the middle, below the middle, the top, the bottom above the bars, left and right of the middle. After each step the row shows for a few seconds, even with no buff missing, so you can see where it is. Shift-drag still places it anywhere with a mouse.

## 0.11.0

- New: **missing buffs**. A row of glowing icons near the middle of the screen shows the self-buffs your class should have up but does not (for example Inner Fire and Power Word: Fortitude, Arcane Intellect and an armor, an aspect, Battle Shout, a shaman's shield and weapon imbue), or that have under 2 minutes left (30 seconds for short buffs). Click an icon to cast it on yourself. Only learned spells are asked for, any version of a buff counts (any armor, the group Fortitude), and it stays quiet while mounted, dead or on a flight. In combat it waits, as the game allows no changes then. Shift-drag to move it; turn it off with the new tick box in the window or `/macrokit buffs`.

## 0.10.1
